correctness.rationale: Forced nonoverlined appearances give the exact square-plus-even-triangle removal bijection. Log-concavity and nonnegative weighted survival sums give negative quadrant dependence and strict squared-gap covariance for n>=4. Classical overpartition Rademacher asymptotics give uniform f second derivative -pi/(4n^(3/2)); a mixed double integral, a marginal exponential tail bound and two explicit weighted Gaussian Riemann sums produce -4/pi^3 times sqrt n. All quantifier/boundary cases are stated; finite checker results are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The specific joint statistic and its sharp mixed covariance coefficient were not found in examined full-text parity-restricted mex literature, prior published analytic ingredients, semantic mathematical records or accessible current-week historical claims. Prior single-mex/curvature tools are explicitly acknowledged and unindexed/general-theorem priority uncertainty remains. Compared Bhoria, Eyyunni and Santra (2026), which has primary 11P83 and counts missing-part multiplicities but not the two-parity nonoverlined joint gaps.
residual_risks: Earlier general random-partition conditional dependence theorem may imply the same mixed covariance without naming these gaps.
Research records are incomplete; accessible current-week historical claims were compared but unavailable prior-week ledgers were not represented as checked.
Published main-term and log-concavity ingredients mean the result is a new synthesis, not a new analytic partition counting method.

value.rationale: Quantifies the first negative dependence correction remaining after asymptotic independence of two natural parity-restricted missing-part statistics. The exact finite survival law and -4/pi^3 covariance constant distinguish joint dependence from already known marginal mex identities; the motivated model originates in active 2025–2026 overpartition parity-statistics research.
